SEC25A-01.note: 'Cattle' is plural and the conditional 'provided that ... comes' plus 'let' set present tense, so 'are safe'. 'is/was' tempt only readers who treat 'cattle' as a mass noun; 'were' tempts as a hypothetical.

SEC25A-02.note: 'Each X and Y' takes a singular verb, and 'before the growers recognized' sets past: 'was developing'. 'were developing' is attractive because of the compound subject and the plural 'trays'.

SEC25A-03.note: Singular head 'comparison' and a specific past time ('on the third day of that year's monsoon') require simple past 'was halted'. 'were halted' draws on 'candidates'; 'has been' conflicts with a dated past event.

SEC25A-04.note: VP ellipsis of 'has withstood' needs the perfect auxiliary in plural: 'have not'. 'has not' is pulled by the singular 'it' right before the blank; 'do not' is plural but cannot stand in for a perfect-tense antecedent.

SEC25A-05.convention: pronoun-antecedent agreement: 'their' has a grammatical plural antecedent ('nurses'); only world inference (the flooding clinic's fridge) prefers 'its'
SEC25A-05.note: Plural 'nurses' needs 'have moved'; 'its' refers to the clinic whose flooding motivates the move. But 'their vaccine refrigerator' (the outreach nurses' own fridge) is grammatical and not contradicted by the text, so the pronoun half is not exclusive.
SEC25A-05.drop_reason: Not exclusive: 'have moved their' has a grammatical plural antecedent ('nurses'), and only a world inference (the fridge was the flooding clinic's) rules it out; the authored claim that the nurses 'were not flooded' does not show their fridge was not at the clinic.

SEC25A-06.note: Plural 'health workers' takes 'carry'; the thing carried is the one heat-stable cholera vaccine, 'it'. 'them' could reach for 'three oral vaccines' but the next sentence puts the other two in cold boxes; 'carries' is pulled by 'district'.

SEC25A-07.note: The verb is 'recurred' (participle, seven words later), so the auxiliary must be 'has', singular for 'dermatitis'. 'have' is pulled by 'patches'/'wrists'; 'is/are' fail only once the far participle is found.

SEC25A-08.note: Blood was drawn in all four barns, so the participial phrase restricts which samples were retested: no punctuation. A comma or dash (A, B) is grammatical but makes the phrase nonrestrictive, saying all samples came from that barn; D splits 'drawn' from its complement and is struckable.

SEC25B-01.note: Singular head 'atlas' and present 'turns out' give 'is revised'. 'are revised' draws on 'trails'.

SEC25B-02.note: Plural 'mains' and the dated past 'at the height of last winter's cold snap' require 'were losing'. 'was losing' is pulled by 'reservoir'/'hospital'; the perfect forms clash with a specific past time.

SEC25B-03.note: Singular 'seismometer' with simultaneous present 'sort out' gives 'is being calibrated'. 'were/are' draw on 'aftershocks'; 'was' ignores the present 'while' clause.

SEC25B-04.note: Plural 'teams' takes 'are'; the emissions belong to the erupting vent, 'its'. 'their' could tempt toward the teams or the (inactive) older craters.

SEC25B-05.note: Forward (cataphoric) ellipsis of 'discharge water at a nearly constant rate' needs do-support in singular: 'does not'. 'was not' is attractive because the last sentence narrates the geyser in past tense, but 'be' cannot stand in for 'discharge'; 'do not' is pulled by 'springs'.

SEC25B-06.note: Singular 'glare' with past 'struck' gives 'was dangerous'. 'were' draws on 'panels'.

SEC25B-07.note: Compound subject 'a technician and two engineers' is plural ('were'); the object covered is the dish, 'it'. 'was' tempts readers who stop at 'a technician'; 'them' reaches for 'wind farms'.

SEC25B-08.note: 'a crescent ... drew climbers' is an independent clause, so a semicolon. The comma (A) is attractive because 'a crescent of bare rock' first reads as an appositive to 'scar' until 'drew' arrives; the colon is weak because the second clause does not explain the first.

SEC25C-01.note: Compound 'the fresco and the gilded screen' is plural; 'each winter unless ... are moved' is present: 'are blackening'. 'is' draws on 'chancel'.

SEC25C-02.note: Singular 'rivalry' with habitual present 'after the judges have read out' gives 'is reported'. 'are' draws on 'bands'; past forms tempt from 'outlived'.

SEC25C-03.note: Singular 'portrait' and a closed past span ('during the decades after the painters' deaths') require 'was obscure'. 'were' draws on 'sisters'; 'has been' wrongly extends the span to now.

SEC25C-04.note: Plural 'townspeople' takes 'were'; they defended the porch/cathedral, 'its'. 'their' is attractive by matching the plural subject or the canons, but the townspeople opposed the canons.

SEC25C-05.note: Singular 'restorer' takes 'has'; what is uncovered is the frescoes, 'them'. 'it' tempts toward 'apse' or 'whitewash'; 'have' is pulled by 'frescoes'.

SEC25C-06.note: Ellipsis of 'was structurally sound' with plural 'remains': 'were not'. 'was not' draws on 'tower'; 'have/has not' cannot replace a copular past.

SEC25C-07.note: Singular 'chapel' takes 'was'; the visitors are the monks, 'them'. 'were' draws on 'stalls'; 'by it' has no sensible antecedent.

SEC25C-08.note: Two hands and 'Both men' make the possessor plural: 'copyists''. 'copyist's' tempts from 'a hired copyist' earlier; 'copyists work' turns 'work' into a verb and garbles the clause.

SEC25D-01.note: Ellipsis of 'are eligible' with 'the elderly' (plural): 'are not'. 'is not' tempts readers who treat 'the elderly' as singular; 'have/has not' cannot replace a copula.

SEC25D-02.note: Singular 'eye tracker' takes 'follows'; the eyes are the infants', 'their'. 'its eyes' is nonsensical for a tracker, so the pronoun half is nearly free.
SEC25D-02.drop_reason: Too easy for the hard route: 'its eyes' for an eye tracker is nonsense, so the pronoun half is free and the verb half ('eye tracker follows') carries no attractor.

SEC25D-03.note: The inverted 'which language should the merged school teach' is a direct question, so it ends with a question mark before the new sentence. The period (D) is the strongest distractor; A is a comma splice, C fused.

SEC25D-04.note: Plural 'applications' and the past conditional 'If ... reached' require 'were routed'. 'was' draws on 'employer'; perfect forms clash with the past habitual frame.

SEC25D-05.note: Plural 'assignments' with past 'voted' in the unless-clause gives 'were provisional'. 'was' draws on 'charter'; perfect forms clash with 'voted'.

SEC25D-06.note: Singular 'archivist' takes 'is'; the tapes are converted, 'them'. 'it' tempts toward 'trunk'; 'are' is pulled by 'linguists'/'tapes'.

SEC25D-07.note: Singular 'bookkeeper' takes 'was'; the names and amounts are the borrowers', 'their'. 'its' could reach for 'the lender', which is the weaker reading; 'were' draws on 'borrowers'.

SEC25D-08.note: 'Voters never changed mayors' means one mayor for twelve years, so the singular possessive 'mayor's'. 'mayors'' is attractive because 'mayors' is printed in the first sentence and 'plans' is plural.

tells: Verb+pronoun 2x2 grids ALWAYS key a number-mismatched pair (singular verb with plural pronoun or vice versa): SEC25A-05 have/its, SEC25A-06 carry/it, SEC25B-04 are/its, SEC25B-07 were/it, SEC25C-04 were/its, SEC25C-05 has/them, SEC25C-07 was/them, SEC25D-02 follows/their, SEC25D-06 is/them, SEC25D-07 was/their. 10 of 10. A test-taker can strike both number-matched options (e.g. 'is converting it', 'are converting them') without reading, leaving a coin flip, and solving either half alone fully decides.

In tense grids that include present-perfect options (has been/have been), the key is ALWAYS simple past: SEC25A-03, SEC25B-02, SEC25C-03, SEC25D-04, SEC25D-05. The perfect forms are never keyed anywhere in the batch.

The noun printed immediately before the blank disagrees in number with the key in most agreement items (about 17 of 26: e.g. SEC25A-02 trays, SEC25A-03 candidates, SEC25B-01 trails, SEC25B-03 aftershocks, SEC25B-06 panels, SEC25C-02 bands, SEC25C-03 sisters, SEC25C-06 tower, SEC25C-07 stalls, SEC25D-04 employer); 'pick the number opposite the nearest noun' beats chance.
Ellipsis items always key the auxiliary that matches the antecedent verb form (SEC25A-04, SEC25B-05, SEC25C-06, SEC25D-01); once one is learned the others follow.
near_duplicates: verb number plus object pronoun in a 2x2 grid
dated past versus present perfect with number attractor
was/were/is/are grid set by a later tense cue
elliptical auxiliary matching an antecedent verb
possessive number decided by a context count of owners
